name: Field_SceneNode_FlushPositions
summary: Before tearing a field scene node down, copies each record's position (f_9C/f_A0/f_A4) into the save-work's per-object record table (0xB8 stride) when the record's page id f_318 and bytes f_3AA/f_3AB match the node, then releases the two lists, the container at f_3C4 and the handle at f_3E4.
evidence: The table comes from func_00192F78(work+0x24A98); work+0x24A98 is the save work (SaveData_ResetSaveWork), so the copy is a save of field object positions, and Container_ReleaseListAndFree/Field_SceneObject_ReleaseHandleAndEffects confirm the teardown that follows. 'Flush' is the right verb; only the 'which object kind' part stays open.

name: maybe_Ui_Overlay_ReleaseHandle
signature: void maybe_Ui_Overlay_ReleaseHandle(void* self, int arg2, int arg3, int arg4)
summary: Releases the field object handle held in self->stateRecord through Field_ObjectManager ((work+8)->f_54) and resets the item-text window out-animations first, then re-points self+4/self+8 at the two global screen-transition callback slots. Only caller is the still-maybe 0x001E3B40, so the class stays open.
evidence: Body is now clear (Ui_ItemTextWindow_ResetOutAnims + func_001C7570 on the Field_ObjectManager with self->stateRecord), but the owner class is only reached through another maybe_ function and no vtable names it, so no confident upgrade.

name: maybe_Gfx_SpriteObject_ReleaseSceneHandle
summary: Runs the shared base routine 0x00406CB0 and then releases the sprite's scene child handle through Gfx_SpriteObject_ReleaseChildHandle on the scene context. This is a handle-release path, not an event notification, so the old 'OnNotify' wording was misleading.
evidence: Named callees Gfx_GetSceneSpriteContext + Gfx_SpriteObject_ReleaseChildHandle and the self->sceneSpriteContext argument describe a release; the base call 0x00406CB0 is unnamed and there are still no callers, so the class/slot stays tentative.

name: Ui_MemberListWindow_RebuildRows
signature: void Ui_MemberListWindow_RebuildRows(void* memberListWindow, const u8* rowState)
summary: Builds up to four party-member rows from the state record's per-slot bytes, invokes Ui_InvokeRecordCallback for each row, then highlights the first row and re-points the six anim refs at the current row.
evidence: Only caller Ui_MemberListWindow_EnsureRowsBuilt, and the callee set (Ui_InvokeRecordCallback, Ui_Widget_SetNamedPaneText, Ui_AnimRef_ResetPanes, Ui_LayoutObject_Bind) exactly matches building member rows in a list window.

name: Ui_UmaWindow_InitEntryFlags
signature: void Ui_UmaWindow_InitEntryFlags(int* work, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Walks the 256 uma records through 0x0063EFB0 and, for each record whose f_77/f_78 pair passes the visibility check (including the Spirit_CountRosterEntries comparison), sets the matching cup flag in the save work via the save-work vtable setter using g_umaCupFlagTable.
evidence: Caller Ui_UmaWindow_Ctor fixes the screen, and the bodies now show save-work flag ids taken from g_umaCupFlagTable with value 1 - i.e. the window's one-time entry/cup flag initialisation, not generic data setup.

name: Ui_UmaWindow_RegisterCallback
summary: Registers the window in its owner's listener list: links self+0x8F4 into owner+0x2C with the shared intrusive-list helper, copies the listener triple from the g_uiUmaWindowPageSelectTable global, and stores the owner at self+0x8EC.
evidence: Called from Ui_UmaWindow_Ctor and the listener source global is now named g_uiUmaWindowPageSelectTable, so the 'uma window registers its callback' reading is consistent; only the listener role of the global remains inferred.

name: maybe_Ui_ScreenCtor_vt779A7C
summary: Constructor of an arc-list-window screen variant: base-constructs with Ui_ArcListWindow_CtorParts, installs vtable 0x00779A7C (g_uiArcListWindowVtableE), seeds nine floats from g_directionReferenceVector, chains three 0x0049B79C sub-objects and flags the result. The concrete screen is still identified only by its vtable address.
evidence: Caller Ui_ScreenController_InitChildren and base ctor Ui_ArcListWindow_CtorParts are named, but the vtable has no sibling names and no string identifies which screen it is.

name: maybe_Model_Actor_Ctor_Vt77AE38
summary: Constructor of a model-actor variant: base-constructs with Ui_CompositeObject_Ctor (0x002E4A10), installs vtable 0x0077AE38 (g_modelActorVtableB), seeds the zero/direction/basis vectors, copies the battle target-marker params and calls the projection-matrix setup 0x002AEC34.
evidence: The installed vtable global is g_modelActorVtableB and the body copies maybe_g_battleTargetMarkerParams, so the previous 'Ui_SceneObject' label was wrong; the concrete marker class is still unproven (no named vtable siblings).

name: Ui_MessageWindow_DeletingDtorA
summary: Deleting destructor of the first message-window variant: installs g_uiMessageWindow3DNodeVtable plus its secondary table at +0x258, releases the embedded handle at +0x2F4, runs Actor2D_EffectNode_DeletingDtor and frees the block.
evidence: The vtable global is now named g_uiMessageWindow3DNodeVtable and the handle/Pack_Handle_Dtor/Actor2D_EffectNode chain matches the destructor of that class; only the A/B variant distinction is positional.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_DeletingDtorB
summary: Deleting destructor of the second message-window variant: installs g_uiMessageWindow3DNodeVtableB and its secondary table, releases the handle at +0x2FC, runs Actor2D_EffectNode_DeletingDtor and frees the block.
evidence: Same named destructor chain as 0x004E650C on the sibling vtable global g_uiMessageWindow3DNodeVtableB; the variant letter only reflects the two compiled copies.

name: Ui_ListWindow_FillStatRows
signature: void Ui_ListWindow_FillStatRows(void* listWidget, const void* stats, int arg3, void* callback)
summary: Fills list rows from the g_uiItemListRowDescriptor table: for every positive getter value it writes the label (via the UI core string table), a '+D'-formatted number and three separator panes, using the widget's capacity/row-base virtuals and hiding unused rows afterwards.
evidence: The descriptor table is now a named global (g_uiItemListRowDescriptor) and the body is a pure five-pane stat row writer; the only remaining unknown is which screen installs this filler.

name: Ui_ListWindow_FillExtraRows
signature: void Ui_ListWindow_FillExtraRows(void* listWidget, const void* rowSource, unsigned int arg3, void* callback)
summary: Second filler of the same list-window family: selects the extra-row mode via virtual slot +0x14 (argument 1), then writes six panes per row (label, '+D' number, separators, icon id 0xAA) from the g_uiItemListRowDescriptor getters.
evidence: Shares the named descriptor table and the exact skeleton of the confirmed Ui_ListWindow_FillStatRows; the only difference is the mode argument 1 and the extra icon pane.

name: maybe_Svc_ObjectPool_DestroyB
summary: Sends IPC request 0x207 (reported through the error path on failure) and then unlinks the shared-memory entry for the same pool id; called by Text_NgWord_OpenService, i.e. it closes the service state before the open/init path.
evidence: The only caller is Text_NgWord_OpenService and the pool id 0x207 plus Svc_UnlinkSharedEntry fit a service teardown, but nothing in the body names the service, so the 'object pool' wording is still a guess.

name: maybe_Svc_Object_Cmd8
signature: void maybe_Svc_Object_Cmd8(void* object, u32 request, u32 second, u32 third, u32 request2, u32 fifth, u32 flag)
summary: Service-object vtable slot: fetches the checked object handle and forwards six arguments (with the flag replicated into both halves of a word) to Svc_Ipc_Send08030102. The meaning of command 0x08030102 stays unknown.
evidence: Only the two named callees are visible and there are no callers; the command word is unresolved, so no better name than the positional 'Cmd8' is justified.

name: Fs_ArchiveEntry_SeekByMode
signature: int Fs_ArchiveEntry_SeekByMode(void* self, uint32_t where, uint32_t offsetLo, int offsetHi, int mode)
summary: Implements seek modes: 0 = absolute position, 1 = relative to the current position (self[1]/self[2], 64-bit), 2 = end-relative (queries the stream length through 0x00504F78), anything else returns 0xE0E046BD; then delegates to Fs_ArchiveEntry_SetReadPosition.
evidence: Both named callers (Fs_ArchiveEntry_Seek, Fs_ArchiveStream_SeekTo) are seek wrappers and the three modes plus the length query settle the semantics; the CARRY4/unaff code is only Ghidra's 64-bit carry math.

name: Ui_IconCache_CopyNameTag
summary: Copies one 8-byte cache-entry name tag into the caller's record: a non-null source is copied as-is, a null source writes the 0x006722EC initialiser (the 'ERROR   ' tag used by Ui_IconCache_WriteIndexTable). Returns the out pointer.
evidence: Ui_IconCache_WriteIndexTable passes either &g_iconCacheErrorTag or the std_String at entry+0x20, and both are copied as 8 bytes into the index record - the field is a name tag, not a timestamp.

name: maybe_Svc_ContentObject_QueryPresent
summary: Two-step query of a service object: calls virtual slot +0x2C with reply buffers for request bytes 2 and 3, then uses maybe_Svc_ContentObject_QuerySize to fill the cached state and returns the resulting presence/error code. Nothing ties it to the icon cache.
evidence: The only named callee is maybe_Svc_ContentObject_QuerySize and the body is a generic slot+0x2C byte query with a cached state block; the previous Ui_IconCache_IsPresent guess came from the address neighbourhood only.

name: Svc_Blob_Serialize
summary: Serialises a blob into the caller's buffer: copies the 0x70-byte header, writes each block as an 8-byte sub-header plus 4-byte-padded payload, then the main payload and the 0x20-byte trailer; returns the size word at blob+4.
evidence: The body is a complete write-out with memcpy calls at fixed sizes, called by Ui_IconCache_WorkerThread (writing the icon cache file); 'Svc_' only says the blob type is a shared service structure.

name: maybe_Regex_OpReplaceOutputList
signature: u32 maybe_Regex_OpReplaceOutputList(void* cursor, void** out, void** left, void* right)
summary: Regex opcode handler (reached only through the opcode table): with the zero flag it clears the left operand's variant child list and appends one successor value; otherwise it iterates the operand count, builds successor lists through 0x00513FD4 and appends each value to the output.
evidence: No callers (table entry) and the operand roles are still inferred from Container_Variant_AddChild/ClearChildren plus maybe_Regex_BuildSuccessorList; the handler shape is right but the operand meanings are not proven.

name: maybe_Sound_GetDriverParam
signature: int maybe_Sound_GetDriverParam(unsigned paramId, unsigned arg2, unsigned arg3, unsigned arg4)
summary: Reads one signed-byte parameter under the scheduler lock: Os_LockScheduler (0x00119BA8), Gfx_IpcCmd90040(paramId, &out), fatal error path on failure, unlock, return the byte. Called once from Sound_Driver_Init, so it is a driver-parameter query, not a DSP command.
evidence: Body and caller are clear but the command wrapper Gfx_IpcCmd90040 is itself unnamed, so neither the service nor the parameter meaning can be confirmed.

name: maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListR
signature: u32 maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListR(void* self, u32 list, void* particle, int forwarded, u32 forwarded2)
summary: Active-list updater of one emitter type: advances the particle through the Fx_UpdateParticle* helpers, copies the eleven transform/quaternion words into each live child node when the emitter flag 0x40 is set, and tail-jumps to Fx_CommitParticleStream.
evidence: All callees are the Fx particle family and the copy block is now readable, but there are still no callers and the 'R' variant is positional, so the entry point stays tentative.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitterSlot_Allocate
signature: void* maybe_Fx_EmitterSlot_Allocate(void* owner, void* desc, uint32_t kind, uint32_t index, uint32_t sub, uint32_t arg6)
summary: Allocates a 0x5880-byte FX emitter slot: scans the owner's slot table for a free record, links it into the per-channel list, and fills the header (kind, template from desc->emitterTemplate, channel index, default velocity from g_fxParticleDefaultVelocity). Returns null when the pool is exhausted.
evidence: The body reads g_fxParticleNodeAllocCount / g_fxParticleDefaultVelocity and desc->emitterTemplate / channelIndex, which are FX emitter concepts, so the previous 'Mem_PoolSlot' label named the mechanism but not the subsystem; the body is still damaged (bad instruction data).

name: Gfx_ModelPart_AllocSlots
signature: void Gfx_ModelPart_AllocSlots(void* part, u32 base, u32 count, u32 size, u8 mode)
summary: Carves a model instance's per-part tables out of the resource buffer: aligns the size to 0x10, lays out the per-slot 0x448/0xD0 tables for both sub-blocks, then default-constructs the eight 0x20-byte elements of every 0x100-byte block through std_ConstructArray.
evidence: Only caller Gfx_ModelInstance_BuildSubBlocks passes the same base/count/size it uses for its own 0x448-byte sub-block layout, and the fixed strides are visible in the body.

name: maybe_Sound_Stream_QueueWork
signature: void maybe_Sound_Stream_QueueWork(void* item, u32 reserved, u32 reserved2, u32 context)
summary: Prepares a sound work item (clears +0x54, self-links +0x7C/+0x80, copies the queue head from +0x14) and pushes it on the engine job queue under the queue monitor, then signals the queue.
evidence: Callee Sound_Stream_ProcessWork and the Os_LockMonitor/Os_QueueTryPush pair match the documented queue push, but the only caller (0x005543B0) is unnamed and the readable body overruns into the next function.

name: Sound_ChannelGroup_ReleaseVoices
summary: Releases a channel group: for a normal group it stops and frees every channel except keepVoice, for a partial allocation it only clears the matching slot, then it clears the group state, unlinks it from the mixer and invokes the owner callback with reason 3.
evidence: The body indexes the SECOND argument as the group (channel array at +0, count at +8, callback at +0xC) and only compares the first argument against entries, so the previous signature's argument roles were reversed; Sound_Mixer_RelinkVoice and Sound_Channel_SetState confirm the teardown.

name: maybe_Sound_Driver_ClearRunningFlag
summary: One-shot shutdown step: when the driver's +0x1F4 flag is set, marks the driver shut down, calls the Sound_GetSystem thunk and clears +0x1F4. Nothing in the body mentions a timer, so the old 'StopTimer' wording was unsupported.
evidence: Caller Sound_System_Shutdown fixes the shutdown role, but the callee is only a thunk onto Sound_GetSystem whose result is discarded, so what the flag gates remains unknown.

name: Sound_Player_Reset
summary: Resets a player to its idle state: unlinks its two driver-queue nodes, finishes and frees any playing note, clears the active/playing/parameter flags, releases the pending file request and detaches the driver-registry node.
evidence: Sole caller Sound_Player_Ctor calls it before initialising the player's fields, and every branch is teardown of leftover state (Sound_SeqNote_MarkFinished, Sound_Player_UpdateVolumePan, Sound_Voice_TrimPriorityList).

name: Sound_SeqPlayer_ProcessStreamWorkItems
signature: void Sound_SeqPlayer_ProcessStreamWorkItems(void* player, u32 frame, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Consumes the sequence player's completed stream-work entries (state byte 3 at +0x241): accumulates their sample offsets into f_58, rebuilds the channel-slot table, queues follow-up stream work and starts the next batch of voices.
evidence: Caller Sound_Command_ExecuteList plus callees Sound_Stream_QueueWorkItem and Sound_Voice_StartPcmStream and the state-byte loop show stream refill processing rather than 'active note' bookkeeping.

name: maybe_Gfx_SamplerState_Write
summary: Appends a fixed state group to the PICA200 command stream: mode 0 emits element command 0 with bytes 1/0x80/6, modes 1 and 2 emit element command 1 with the filter/wrap bytes swapped, then the three bytes are written and the stream cursor at state+4 is advanced.
evidence: Callers Gfx_SubmitSortedElement and Gfx_Overlay_SubmitQuad plus Gfx_Pica_EmitDrawElements fix the command-stream role, but whether the three bytes are texture-sampler state or another fixed state group is not proven.

name: maybe_Model_BuildAimPartList
signature: void maybe_Model_BuildAimPartList(u32 owner, u32 partA, u32 partB, u32 partC)
summary: Helper of Model_AttachAimParts that default-constructs two 0x40-byte part descriptors in a stack buffer (std_ConstructArray over the 0x00535B54 constructor). Almost all of the 1,992-byte body is lost in the decompilation.
evidence: Only caller Model_AttachAimParts and the single surviving std_ConstructArray call; the descriptor contents and the meaning of the four arguments are unknown.

name: maybe_Container_UnlinkAllNodes
summary: Unlinks a node from its containers: erases the intrusive list range at entry+4, and when the node is marked as tree-linked also erases its red-black-tree node, then returns the entry. A container helper, not an Fs archive deep destructor.
evidence: Body is only Container_List_EraseAllNodes + std_RbTree_EraseNode and returns its argument; nothing refers to archives or Fs, so the previous 'Fs_Entry_Dtor' class label was unsupported (no callers either).

name: maybe_Field_ObjectType_InitRecord
summary: Constructor of a field scene-object variant: allocates the object and two sub-records in one block, installs g_battleSequenceThunkVtable on both sub-records, seeds vectors (zero and one) and creates two sprite objects through Field_ObjectSprite_CtorBase.
evidence: Caller Field_Scene_UpdateObjectsFromTable and the Field_ObjectSprite_CtorBase chain fix the field-object role, but the vtable global (g_battleSequenceThunkVtable) does not name the concrete object type, so 'ObjectType' remains vague on purpose.

name: maybe_Field2D_MapChip_CollectCellsInRect
signature: u64 maybe_Field2D_MapChip_CollectCellsInRect(u32* self, int fromCell, int toCell, int* path, u32 flags)
summary: Collects the map cells inside the target region (Gfx_Scene_FindFirstEntryInRect) that pass the chip condition test and the from-cell region filter, stores them in the caller's array and returns a packed result comparing the collected set with the expected one. There is no path search in the body.
evidence: Callees Gfx_Scene_FindFirstEntryInRect, Field2D_MapChip_IsConditionActive and Field2D_MapChip_ScanColumnToEdge show a filtered rect collection, so 'FindPath' was misleading; the body is still damaged (truncated control flow) and callers are unnamed.

name: Field2D_Sprite_SetAppearanceFromCharId
signature: void Field2D_Sprite_SetAppearanceFromCharId(u32* self, u32 object, u32 arg3, int charId)
summary: Chooses a 2D sprite's appearance from a character id: resolves the character's frame/palette key (0xFF fallback), and either re-runs Field2D_Sprite_ComputeDrawParams or resets the sprite's chip bits and detaches the slot object.
evidence: The body reads the character frame pair through 0x00149814 / 0x0063B944 with the 0xFF fallback and always ends in Field2D_Sprite_ComputeDrawParams, matching the name; no caller names the screen, so it stays at 0.5.

name: Field2D_Sprite_AdvancePathStep
summary: Per-frame path update of a 2D sprite: decrements the step counter at +0x38 and, for each of the two path programs at +0x2D0/+0x2D4, asks 0x00667EA4 for the next step and rebuilds the attached task object.
evidence: Caller Field2D_Sprite_CheckViewBounds, callee maybe_Field2D_Sprite_ChoosePathStep and the two fixed path-program slots make the step-advance reading solid.

name: maybe_Data_GetFirstRowA
summary: Getter whose return Ghidra dropped: resolves Game_GetDataManager and calls the pure table getter 0x0063F7BC on the manager, i.e. returns the first row of the manager's sub-table. The caller (Field_NpcJumpAction_Setup) discards the result, so the table's identity stays unknown.
evidence: Body is two calls with a dropped return; only the caller (jump-action setup) and the manager getter are named, and one of four identical copies cannot be told apart without the caller's use.

name: maybe_Sound_StreamPlayer_InitLock
signature: void maybe_Sound_StreamPlayer_InitLock(void* player, u32 mode, int channelCount, int arg4)
summary: One-time start/lock setup called from Sound_InitPlayers: if the player's flag bit 0 is clear, a channel count was requested and the global stream thread state is free, it initialises the critical section at g_soundStreamThreadStack and stores a thread handle. The tail is lost to bad instruction data.
evidence: Caller Sound_InitPlayers and callees Os_InitCriticalSection / 0x00111288 are the only evidence; halt_baddata truncates the function, so the 'stream player' attribution remains unproven.

name: Gfx_Trail_PushPathNode
signature: void Gfx_Trail_PushPathNode(void* trail, int cellX, int cellY, int force)
summary: Appends a reached cell to the trail's 16-entry path ring at +0xF0 (stride 0xC, index +0x1B0), validating the step with Gfx_Trail_TryConnectCell unless forced, then advancing the ring index capped at 15.
evidence: Caller Gfx_Trail_AdvancePathNode and callee Gfx_Trail_TryConnectCell are named and the ring/cap logic is fully visible; only the post-advance bookkeeping is lost to bad instruction data.

name: maybe_Ui_SceneObject_ReleaseFromCore
summary: Two-call thunk: gets the UI core with Ui_GetCore and calls Ui_SceneObject_Release on it. Used as a callback (its only caller is Sq_HashTable_Remove), so it releases the current core's scene objects rather than orchestrating UI flow.
evidence: Both callees are confident and the argument is only forwarded into Ui_GetCore, so the 'release the core's scene object' reading holds; the callback contract (why Sq_HashTable_Remove reaches it) is still open.

name: Gfx_SceneSpriteSet_SetCharacterId
signature: void Gfx_SceneSpriteSet_SetCharacterId(void* self, unsigned int characterId, unsigned int arg3, int force)
summary: Selects the sprite set's active character id: stores it in scenePresetMode, resolves the 0xD4-stride character record and its f_D1 redirect byte, then re-applies the preset through Gfx_SceneSpriteSet_ApplyPreset when the id changed or force is set.
evidence: The body stores the id, honours the redirect byte and only skips when the active index already matches; the sibling caller Menu_SetSelectedActorId puts it in the character-selection path.

name: Item_SortU16ListByItemKey
signature: void Item_SortU16ListByItemKey(void* work, void* container, u32 sentinelKey)
summary: Sorts the u16 item-id list starting at container+0x3C4 up to the sentinel key (or the work bound) with std_insertion_sort_u16_item, then finishes the order with Item_CompareEntryKey32 comparisons.
evidence: Both sort helpers and Item_CompareEntryKey32 (item sort key) are named, and the three callers (map-chip walk triggers, menu result message) all sort item-id lists before display.

name: maybe_Ui_ListWindow_HandleDetailToggle
summary: For a row with flag bit 2 set: hides the row's child widget and enables the detail panes on the owner at +0x398. The rest of the body is lost to bad instruction data, and there are no callers.
evidence: Only Ui_Widget_SetChildVisible and Ui_ListWindow_ToggleDetailPanes are visible before halt_baddata; no caller or vtable entry ties it to a specific list window.

name: Field_HandleList_Ctor
summary: Constructs a small handle list: installs g_fieldHandleListVtable, allocates an 8-byte allocator wrapper (g_battlePopupPoolVtable) and a 0x94-byte reader object built by 0x0058C40C, so the list owns the allocator/reader pair.
evidence: The installed vtable global is named g_fieldHandleListVtable and the two allocations are now readable; the two callers (Ui3D_InitEffectPairFromRecord, field spawn) both need a handle list.

name: Battle_Unit_ValidateTarget
summary: Validates a battle target: finds the unit in the table at self+0xE8 (stride 0x2C8), resolves its action row through the data manager (0x0063FC70/0x0063FD24) and returns 0/1/2 by comparing slot, group and ten stat fields against the action's target criteria.
evidence: Callers Battle_SelectAiActions (choosing a target) and Battle_ActionModel_UpdateAttachmentVisibility (marker visibility) plus the ten field comparisons make target validation the only consistent reading.

name: Field_CanUpdateCameraTargetActor
summary: Returns 1 when there is no camera-target actor ((work+8)->f_54->+0x1C) or Field_Actor_CanUpdate accepts it, and the global motion-set flag g_fieldActorCanUpdateMotionSetFlag is set; otherwise 0.
evidence: Body reads exactly the camera-target actor slot documented for (work+8)->f_54 and tests the now-named global g_fieldActorCanUpdateMotionSetFlag; the sole caller is the pose-anim update.

name: maybe_Ui_Plate_ResolvePlayerTitle
summary: Resolves a nameplate's player title: looks up the plate record, maps its kind byte (0/1/2) to one of the three g_uiPlatePlayerTitleStrPtrA/B/C strings and checks the party entry (style byte 0x80 -> party type 0x52) to return 0/1/2. It selects a title, it does not format one.
evidence: Caller Ui_PlateWidget_BindEntry and the kind-byte dispatch are clear; the returned 0/1/2 and the bracket style fields are still unexplained, so 'Format' was too specific and the name is softened.

name: maybe_DataTable_IsIndexValidA
summary: Bounds check over a data-manager table: when the kind byte at plate[0] is below 0x1F it fetches the table header with 0x0063F93C and returns 0 if plate[4] is below the header's first limit word, else 1.
evidence: Only caller Party_BuildUsedCharacterList; the comparison direction is now readable, but the header getter is a mid-function label so the table identity is still unproven.

name: maybe_DataTable_GetEntryA
summary: Table accessor: resolves the header with 0x0063F93C, follows its +4 relative pointer and returns the 5-byte-stride entry selected by plate[4].
evidence: Only caller Party_BuildUsedCharacterList; the pointer arithmetic is clear but the section's meaning and the header getter remain unnamed.

name: maybe_Placement_TestCellFree
summary: Resolves the per-record placement handler through maybe_Field_Placement_GetDefaultArea(record[4]), calls it with (record[0], record[1], record+2, point) and returns the inverted result, so 1 means 'cell is free'.
evidence: Both callers (Ui_PlaceWidgetInFreeCell, Field_FindFreePlacementCell2D) break on a 1, so the inverted-result contract holds; the handler table itself is still a maybe_, which is why the 'Ui_' prefix was dropped (it is a shared field/UI placement test).

name: Item_GetGroupColorTag
signature: void Item_GetGroupColorTag(u32* out, u32 not, u16 itemId)
summary: Writes one of two text-colour tags from g_itemCategoryTextColorTable into *out: an item counts as grouped when its record is missing or Item_IsSiblingRecord says the next id belongs to the same group; the 0xFFFF 'no mapping' value from 0x00381938 selects the fallback colour.
evidence: The table is now named g_itemCategoryTextColorTable and the caller Ui_Window_UpdateCursorKind uses the value to colour the cursor row, so the result is a colour tag (the old 'GroupTag' wording hid that).

name: maybe_Gfx_CmdBuf_CopyMarkedBlocks
signature: void* maybe_Gfx_CmdBuf_CopyMarkedBlocks(uint32_t* dst, const uint32_t* src, int size)
summary: Copies command-buffer blocks of 0x80 words, writing a 0xEAD0FEAD marker after each 0x1FC-byte payload and a length-tagged header for the tail block, and returns the new write cursor.
evidence: Marker, payload size and header packing are all visible, so the block-copy role is solid; there are no callers and the only callee (Gfx_GpuCmd_WriteTextureUnits) is unnamed, hence no upgrade.

name: maybe_Gfx_MeshChunk_WritePartMatrices
signature: void maybe_Gfx_MeshChunk_WritePartMatrices(void* self, unsigned int** out, void* parts, void* buf, void* tag)
summary: Writes part matrices into the draw command stream in one of three forms: a single 0x30-byte matrix DMA bind, a gathered multi-matrix staging block, or a palette-merged matrix array; the form is chosen by the low flag bits of the part list.
evidence: The body is a complete 0x30-stride matrix staging/emit path, but its 16 named callers are all UI layout/animation code (Ui_AnimRef_*, Ui_SpriteCache_LookupOrLoad), so the 'mesh chunk' class label is still unproven even though the emitted data is matrix data.

name: Sound_SeqParam_GetRangePair
signature: unsigned int Sound_SeqParam_GetRangePair(void* accessor, unsigned int paramId, unsigned int* outRange)
summary: Combines the base sequence data range from Sound_Seq_GetDataRange with extension vtable slot +0x28 for one sequence parameter, returning the OR of both halves.
evidence: Caller Sound_SeqParam_NotifyChange and callee Sound_Seq_GetDataRange are both named and the OR-combination with the extension slot is unambiguous.

name: Sound_SeqParam_ApplyTimestamp
summary: Reads the base sequence object's track offset via Sound_Seq_GetTrackOffsetBase and forwards it with the caller's value to the enabled extension's vtable slot +0x50.
evidence: Caller Sound_Voice_StartPlayback and callee Sound_Seq_GetTrackOffsetBase are named, and the body only adds the extension-slot dispatch.

name: Sound_Stats_SumPending

name: Field2D_Scene_GetStyleByte18

name: maybe_Text_SpanCursor_ClampLine

name: maybe_Work_RowIdIsNamed

name: maybe_Field2D_Map_MarkLayerFlag

name: maybe_Gfx_RenderCallback_Dispatch
summary: Invokes the runtime-installed callback at g_vramAllocatorC+4: once with no arguments when node->f_4 is set, then once with the node. Both callers are teardown paths (Gfx_ReleaseDeviceObject, Gfx_StreamSlot_Shutdown), so it looks like a 'node is being released' notification.

name: maybe_Movie_SetStreamAllocator

name: Field_ResetLocatorDefaults
summary: Resets a field placement/locator record to defaults: detaches its old target at f_174, clears the 31-char name with std_FixedString31_Ctor, sets the id/offset words (f_17C..f_19C) to 0xFFFF, copies the identity 4x3 matrix into f_1A0..f_1CC, zeroes the vector and sets state f_1DC to 3.

name: maybe_Container_Node_DtorA
summary: Deleting destructor of a node class: installs the vtable g_osSequenceTaskBaseVtable, erases the inline tree node at +0x1C when linked, unlinks two intrusive list heads and frees the block. One of four byte-identical copies.
evidence: The installed vtable global is now readable as g_osSequenceTaskBaseVtable, which hints at an os::SequenceTask base, but the body is a generic container-node teardown and no caller or vtable-sibling name confirms the class.

name: maybe_Container_Node_DtorB
summary: Same deleting destructor as 0x001C635C, emitted a second time for the same class (vtable g_osSequenceTaskBaseVtable): tree-node erase, two list unlinks, operator delete.

name: maybe_Container_Node_DtorC
summary: Third copy of the same deleting destructor (vtable g_osSequenceTaskBaseVtable): tree-node erase, two list unlinks, operator delete.

name: maybe_Container_Node_DtorVtableSlot1
summary: Same container-node deleting destructor as 0x001C635C and literally slot 1 of vtable 0x007824E0; its two callers are Ui_Label_SetFromShortTriple and Field_Actor_UpdateEquipDisplay, which do not fit a sequence-task class.

name: maybe_Field_Talk_StartCameraTransition
summary: State-entry helper for a talk/scene setup: clears +0x15D0, arms a 3.0f timer at +0x15D4, and when the deadline at +0x15E0 is below f_4C sets f_50=1 and copies f_44 into the timer; a set byte at +0x15DC applies the default camera/layout entries, then sets f_29=1 and f_28=0.

name: Object_DeletingDtorWithVtable
summary: Shared scalar deleting destructor stub: installs the caller-supplied vtable in *object, runs the shared base destructor 0x00294C88 and frees the block with operator delete.

name: Object_DeletingDtorWithVtableB
summary: Second compiled copy of the shared scalar deleting destructor: installs the passed vtable, runs base destructor 0x00294C88 and frees with operator delete.

name: maybe_Field_Action_DtorDeleteC

name: Object_DeletingDtorWithVtableC
summary: Third compiled copy of the shared scalar deleting destructor: installs the passed vtable, runs base destructor 0x00294C88 and frees with operator delete.

name: maybe_Ui_ShopWindow_OnConfirm
summary: Confirm/advance handler: reads two flag words from the UI core's controllers (UI_GetCore -> +0x14/+0x10 and +0x1C), and when their AND is non-zero plays animator animation 0xD (or 0x11 with state byte 6 when the window has a pending child at +0x140), then always returns 1.

name: Gfx_SceneNode_UpdateChildClipEvent

name: Gfx_SceneNode_DtorDeleteAlt
summary: Second compiled copy of the Gfx scene-node deleting destructor: releases the child tree through the Field_SceneObject_Delete inner routine 0x005F8528 and frees the object with operator delete.
evidence: Byte-identical to the confident Gfx_SceneNode_DtorDelete at 0x00577740 and sited in the same vtable row next to Gfx_Node_Dtor; renamed with an Alt suffix to avoid duplicating the primary name.

name: Battle_UiRow_UpdateEntryState
summary: Battle list-row update: looks the row's unit (ownerUnit->f_273) up in the two battle unit lists (+0x4254/+0x4270); if present it either plays actor animation 0x2F or calls the owner's vtable+0x84 with a fixed descriptor, otherwise it does nothing.

summary: Validates the actor handle at self->targetActor and then calls 0x005E7848(targetActor, 0); a duplicate copy of 0x00322884 in the sibling vtable 0x007639F0.

name: Field_Marker_CtorVariantC

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_DeletingDtor

name: maybe_Ui_SoulWindow_Subwidget_Ctor

name: maybe_Field_ActorAction_DtorDeleteH
summary: Three-instruction deleting destructor: shared teardown 0x00193E40 then operator delete 0x0010F6CC. No caller and no vtable entry, so the owning class (the H suffix) is positional only.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_DtorDeleteB
summary: Deleting destructor: calls the class destructor 0x0028EFB4 (Actor2D_EffectNode_DeletingDtor) then operator delete.

name: Field_HandleRef_DtorListBase
summary: Non-deleting base destructor: when the link byte at +0x10 is set, erases the object's red-black-tree/list node through 0x0010EC00 + std_RbTree_EraseNode, then returns the object. The base half of the Field_HandleRef destructor pair (vtable 0x00775534).

name: maybe_Fs_StartAsyncRead

name: maybe_Object_ResolveEntryZero
summary: When the object has a container handle at +0xC, its type word at +0x38 is one of three baked class constants (0x00286E68 / 0x00287794 / 0x00286D68) and its sub-index at +0x3C is 0, resolves entry 0 of that container through 0x007133F0.

summary: Byte-identical second copy of 0x00632AF0: same three class constants and the same 0x007133F0 entry-0 lookup; Ui_ScreenFade_Setup calls both copies back to back.

name: maybe_Gfx_Node_InitInlineListA

name: maybe_Actor_ApplyStateFlags

summary: Applies a pending request/state flag block to an actor: sets the facing byte f_7C, copies the shadow/offset pair when bit 0x40 is set, clears the handled bits from actor->f_6C and re-queues the remainder under the global mutex.

name: maybe_Os_SetRuntimeFlag
summary: Takes the runtime mutex and sets a single engine runtime flag byte (g_engineRuntimeFlags+1) to 1; the flag's meaning is unknown and there are no callers.

name: maybe_Snd_BeginFrame
summary: Stream-context frame prologue: re-initialises the csnd stream context, publishes the current buffer pointer, clears the transfer state words, issues a data-synchronisation barrier and takes the context mutex.

name: maybe_Snd_InitDspTimeouts

name: maybe_Gfx_InitE8Record
summary: Zeroes the ten leading words of a 0xE8-byte record and memsets the two 0x60-byte buffers at +0x28 and +0x88; called twice by the engine-startup record-pair constructor.

name: Snd_ResetChannelUnitsToDefault
summary: Writes 0xFFFF into the filter-info and filter-coefficient fields of both channel units and re-submits them through Snd_SetChannelMaskedFields / maybe_Snd_SetChannelDescriptor; one step of stream-context setup.

name: Snd_ResetChannelUnits

summary: Fills a 12-byte parameter block with the given byte, then clears the filter-info and filter-coefficient halfwords of both channel units (from the 0x7F2BA0 state getter) and re-submits them with mask 1.

name: maybe_Gfx_WaitGpuEventLoop
summary: GPU transfer wait loop: repeatedly calls Gfx_TransferGpuBuffer with a cache-flush range and a completion callback, returning early on error or once command buffer 3 reports the finished transfer, otherwise retrying. The loop condition uses a lost flag register (unaff_r9), so the retry exit is inferred, not proven.
evidence: The recovered body is a retry loop around the named Gfx_TransferGpuBuffer with the completion callback at +0x48, which supports the wait reading; but Ghidra lost the r9 flag register that governs the inner loop, so confidence stays low.

name: maybe_Mem_PoolInitFragment

evidence: The body is a pool-fragment reset, but the recovered decompilation carries a coprocessor_store(0) and the pool owner is unnamed, so the name stays tentative.

name: maybe_Snd_IpcCmd17
summary: Parameterless IPC request: writes a command header into the thread command buffer at +0x80, issues svc 0x32 and returns the response word from +0x84 on success.

name: maybe_Gfx_CmdList_PushTextureRows
signature: void maybe_Gfx_CmdList_PushTextureRows(u32 cmdWord, u32 count, const u32* src)
summary: Appends raw data rows to the GPU command list in chunks of at most 0x80 words, writing ((n-1)<<20)|0xF0000|cmdWord headers and copying the pixels, and resets the write pointer to the buffer end on overflow.

name: maybe_Video_ConvertBlocks32_A
